posts.text:
Your colleague smells of alcohol on shift. Do you report it?

Report it. Practising while intoxicated can be a legal duty to notify the regulator. It is about patient safety, not punishment. Write down what you saw, factually, and never treat it as an HR matter only.

Would you A) speak to them privately first, or B) escalate and notify? Reply A or B.

More free practice questions, no sign-up: https://www.nclexready.com.au/sample-questions?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=reel&utm_campaign=post-12

A near miss. No one was hurt. Do you report it?

Report it. Near misses are reported precisely because no one was hurt this time. The review looks for system causes, not blame. If harm happens, explain honestly, apologise and say what will change. An apology is generally not an admission of liability.

Have you seen a near miss go unreported? A) yes B) no. Reply A or B.

Find your weak areas free: https://www.nclexready.com.au/diagnostic?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=reel&utm_campaign=post-13
